placements.why: The envelope's entire content is an observatory calibration record: an instrument (Kestrelwood spectrograph) checked at a specific frequency against a named reference standard (June reference plates) and confirmed to hold. Neither the supplied strata list (empty for this repo) nor any narrative structure (also empty) offers a home for this organizational activity, and it is distinct in kind from strategy, product, architecture, or proof categories — it is a verification-against-standard activity. No existing name is even close, so this is a NEW mint rather than an INSPIRED one; 'Calibration' names the category the content itself calls for, matching the shape of the org's known top-level taxonomy without requiring any sibling or ancestor to already exist.

placements.why: All three segments describe the same recurring subject: a named instrument's calibration value, checked against a dated reference standard, found to hold. This is true beyond the words describing this one event — future envelopes will keep feeding this same theme with other instruments, other reference sets, other calibration values and outcomes (holds / drifts / fails). The specific numbers (88.4 MHz, June plates, Kestrelwood) are the evidence, not the leaf itself, per the narrative grain test; the leaf is the recurring practice of verifying calibration against a standing reference. src-1 states it in prose, src-2 and src-3 restate the same instrument/calibration facts as structured field labels — all pointing the same direction with no tension, matching the single KestrelwoodCalibrationVerified position already surfaced. Nothing in the (empty) existing narrative structure covers this, so it is minted fresh under the newly-minted Calibration strata.
